newsitem.title: FRANCE: UNIP sees lower protein content in French pea crop.
newsitem.headline: UNIP sees lower protein content in French pea crop.

text.p: Initial results from a survey carried out by the French protein pea producers' federation UNIP suggest the 1996 pea crop may contain less protein than the 1995 crop, producers said on Thursday.
In a note to operators, UNIP linked the decline to a prolonged drought in the spring that curbed nitrogen content in peas.
Field peas are used as a source of protein in animal feed.
Testing of 148 samples showed an average nitrogen weight of 236 grammes for one kilo of dried pea against 250 g in 1995 and 240 g in 1994.

Regions included in the survey showed nitrogen weights ranging from 230 to 240 g, with the exception of the Poitou-Charentes and the Nord-Pas-de-Calais regions that had nitrogen weights close to 250 g.
UNIP cautioned the results of the survey were provisional. It said it would release final and detailed data by regions in its next report.
France may harvest 2.57 million tonnes of field peas in 1996, down 180,000 tonnes from 1995, mainly because farmers sowed less peas, UNIP has said.
